issues.claim: Audit opener: "every appointment is still confirmed by a staff call-back."
issues.problem: Overstated. The appointment-request page only says a team member will contact the client to confirm availability for requests submitted through the web form. Phone bookings are scheduled live on the call and never need a call-back. A practice owner can rebut this sentence in one line, which weakens the paragraph it sits in. BLOCKING.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "web-form appointment requests still wait for a staff call-back" (and, if wanted, "phone bookings are handled live at the desk").

issues.claim: Audit section 2: "housecalls and medical boarding have no booking route beyond the general form or phone."
issues.problem: Contradicted by the cited FAQ page, which lists email as a third way to schedule ("calling ..., completing our online New Client Form, or contacting our office via email"), and by the audit's own preceding sentence, which already names a Gmail address as an intake channel. Internal inconsistency plus an inaccurate limit. BLOCKING.
issues.fix: Change to "no booking route of their own beyond the general phone, form and email channels" — keeps the real point (no dedicated housecall or boarding scheduling path) without the false 'phone and form only' limit.

issues.problem: Body runs roughly 470 words including headings and the closing "Prepared from publicly available information..." line (about 430 words of prose alone), i.e. slightly over the ~450-word ceiling. Non-blocking but worth a trim.
issues.fix: Cut ~25 words: shorten the "Why this works" bullets to one line each, or drop "no preparation needed" from the first-step line, to land at or under 450 including headings.

issues.problem: Accreditation rests on a single third-party job board (iHireVeterinary), which does say "AAHA accredited". The practice's own homepage only says it is a member of the American Animal Hospital Association, and AAHA's hospital locator could not be opened to confirm accreditation independently. Non-blocking, but the strongest available primary source says 'member', not 'accredited'.
issues.fix: Either attribute it ("AAHA-accredited per its company profile") or use the practice's own wording ("AAHA-member practice") to stay inside what its site states.

issues.problem: The $1,500 floor is reachable from the stated assumptions only if unstated per-question handling time (~5 minutes) is included; the hire-rampup math alone recomputes to roughly $400–$2,200 at the cited NJ wages. The audit does show assumptions for opportunities 1 and 2 but not for this one, so the floor looks firmer than it is. Non-blocking (the section already calls the recurrence an inference and points to ramp-up/logs as the real value).
issues.fix: Add a short parenthetical, e.g. "(2–4 hires × 30–60 hrs of colleague time, 30–40% avoided, plus 1–3 questions per staff member per week at ~5 min each, NJ assistant/technician wages)", or lower the floor to $1,000.

issues.problem: Could not be re-verified: linkedin.com returned HTTP 403 for both attempts. Not contradicted — the researcher's profile records the same figure — but it is a precise headcount from a self-reported directory and is the only unverified number in the opener. Non-blocking.
issues.fix: Hedge to "LinkedIn shows about a dozen employees" (or "roughly a dozen staff"), which stays true under small directory drift.
